title: Confidentiality of suspicious activity reports
definition: The rule that the existence of a suspicious activity report, and the information it contains, may not be disclosed to a customer, a suspect or the wider organisation except in the limited ways the rule allows, and the safe harbour for a person who voluntarily discloses information from a report to a law enforcement agency. The confidentiality rule is a reason a report is not explained to a customer, and it is not a licence to mislead one about an unrelated matter.
evidence_to_cite: the report identifier, and the basis on which its existence was disclosed to anyone
the disclosure itself, where one was made, and to whom
the rationale given to the customer for the account's treatment

sources.citation: Confidentiality of suspicious activity reports and the related safe harbour (31 CFR 1020.320), summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.

notes: This record is the one most often misused. The rule restricts what may be said about the report; it does not authorise any other misstatement to the customer.
